newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai telephone firms Q3 earnings seen sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Thai telephone firms Q3 earnings seen sluggish.

text.p: Thailand's fixed-line telephone operators are expected to report sluggish profits in the third quarter due to slow demand and the heavy cost of installation, analysts said on Wednesday.
"We see the subscription of new telephone lines is very slow," said one telecom analyst at a foreign brokerage.
"So I don't expect their earnings will be much different from what they were in the previous quarter."
There are currently two fixed-line operators in Thailand, TelecomAsia Plc and Thai Telephone and Telecommunication Plc.
TelecomAsia Plc, which won the concession to install 2.6 million telephone lines in Bangkok and nearby provinces, said earlier this month only 1.13 million of the lines were subscribed.
Thai Telephone and Telecommunication has a concession to install 1.5 million telephones lines in provincial areas. The company says so far it has connected 853,300 lines.
Both companies were forced to speed up installation to meet the government's deadline of September 30, analysts said.
They expected higher installation costs to affect the companies' third-quarter results.
"There would be an extra cost from the acceleration of the line installation. This will also be included in their third-quarter accounts," said an analyst at Wall Street Finance and Securities.
Analysts expect Thai Telephone and Telecommunication's profit in the third quarter to be lower than in the previous quarter.

Thai Telephone posted a net profit of 194 million baht ($7.76 million) in the second quarter compared with 234 million in the same quarter last year. Its six-month profit totalled 348 million baht against 454 million in the same period last year.
TelecomAsia is expected to report a loss in the quarter due partly to continued losses from its cable TV unit, Universal Television (UTV).

TelecomAsia posted a second quarter loss of 260 million baht compared with a profit of 233 million in the same quarter a year ago. The company saw a loss of 187.5 million in the first six months of the year compared with a profit of 648 million in the same period last year.
